questions.prompt: According to the FLP Impossibility Theorem (Fischer, Lynch, Paterson, 1985), why is deterministic consensus impossible in a purely asynchronous system?
options: Network latency is strictly bounded, creating clock drift
It cannot guarantee both safety and liveness in the presence of even a single unannounced crash failure
Byzantine nodes can forge cryptographic digital signatures
Three-phase commit requires a centralized coordinator
questions.explanation: FLP proves that in a purely asynchronous network, no deterministic protocol can guarantee both safety and liveness if even one node may suffer an unannounced crash failure.

questions.prompt: In the Raft consensus algorithm, when is a log entry considered safely committed by the leader?
options: Immediately when written to the leader's local write-ahead disk log
When all cluster nodes reply with AppendEntries confirmation
When the entry created by the current leader has been replicated on a majority of servers
After the randomized election timeout has expired without a candidate split
questions.explanation: In Raft, a leader commits an entry from its current term once it has successfully replicated that entry on a majority (quorum) of cluster nodes.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate Lamport clocks from Vector clocks
questions.prompt: If Lamport timestamps for two events satisfy L(a) < L(b), this proves event a causally preceded event b (a -> b).
questions.explanation: False. Lamport clocks guarantee that if a -> b then L(a) < L(b), but the converse does not hold. Events may be concurrent even if one has a smaller timestamp.

questions.learningObjective: Explain concurrency detection in Vector Clocks
questions.prompt: Explain how vector clocks detect that two events a and b are concurrent (a || b) rather than causally related.
questions.rubric: Must state that neither vector dominates the other: neither V(a) <= V(b) nor V(b) <= V(a). One coordinate is greater in a while another coordinate is greater in b.
